text:
liam: Quick datapoint from us-west1-provision — after yesterday's driver+firmware bundle (r456 / fw2.3.1) rolled to 6 hosts in pool-g4-usw1 we saw a ~30% drop in Xid fatal spikes overall, but 2 cards (host-g4-072, host-g4-089) started emitting more ECC corrected events. putting notes + a short proposal here.

sasha: Which hosts exactly and can you paste the small excerpt of the logs? :eyes:

liam: hosts: host-g4-067, -072, -078, -081, -089, -094. sample grep:```
$ journalctl -u redwood-inference -n 200 | grep -Ei "xid|ecc"
Mar 16 22:13:01 host-g4-072 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, PID=4120, GPU=0
Mar 16 22:13:01 host-g4-072 redwood-agent: [telemetry] nvml ecc cec: corrected 12
Mar 16 22:14:08 host-g4-089 kernel: NVRM: GPU ecc correctable error on GPU 1
```

ajay: Interesting — Xid down is good. Are the ECCs persistent (same GPU index) or switching? also what workloads were running during the window (long context chat loads or short inferences)?

liam: ECCs are persistent on GPU 0 of -072 and GPU 1 of -089 across the 6h sweep. Both hosts were running mixed workloads (kv-llm batch + streaming chat). Sequence distribution skewed to shorter contexts but occasional 4k bursts.

maria: Given corrected ECCs on stable index + persistent behavior, i'd prefer to drain those two GPUs and run a stress/pmem repro before hardware replacement. spare capacity in us-west1 is tight this week — cost to repro + rebuild ~3 reserved-hours per host if we shift traffic. alternatives?

ajay: Plan suggestion: 1) enable nvml pmon + increase ECC sampling (agent flag: `NVML_ECC_SAMPLING=1`) 2) run targeted synthetic harness for 2h that cycles sequence lengths 512->4096 to exercise VRAM paths 3) capture `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=ecc.errors.uncorrected,ecc.errors.corrected --format=csv` every 30s 4) if we see rising uncorrected or new Xid, mark card for RMA.

infra-bot: Autoscaler: added 2 hosts to pool-g4-usw1 at 2026-03-17T09:14Z to cover drains (ids: host-g4-102, host-g4-103).

liam: I started the sampling script on -072 and -089 (pid 6882). small diff from usual: driver reports `gpu-link: fast-fail disabled` for -089 which we haven't seen in older bundles. logging attached here (short).

sasha: Can we run the repro on ephemeral spare hosts instead of draining production cards immediately? prefer to avoid node replacement if it's just a corrected ECC noise increase. Maria's rebuild estimate feels high.

maria: If repro on spares reproduces the ECC delta -> we still need to decide RMA vs firmware rollback. rollback is low-cost but we lose the Xid reduction gains seen elsewhere. RMA has capital + scheduling hit. If repro fails to reproduce, we'll return cards to prod.

liam: Proposal decision: run 2-hr synthetic on new spares (host-g4-102/103) with the exact image & driver/fw bundle used on the 6 hosts, attach `pmon` and `nv-hostengine` traces, and collect `dmesg` + `nvml` stats. If reproducible within 2h -> schedule RMA for physical card; if not reproducible -> keep in pool and escalate to driver vendor with traces. Also hold full fleet rollout until we verify the remaining hosts for 72h.

ajay: sgtm. add a perf-cost note: running the repro on spares + extra telemetry will add ~0.6 GPU-hours per repro run and increase S3 logs by ~1.2GB. fine but flagging for finance.

sasha: :thumbsup: start the repro and paste the small run link here when ready.

liam: started at 09:20Z on 102/103; test harness name `ecc-smoke-2026-03-17`. I'll post the condensed run output in ~2h. tagging @maria @ajay for visibility.

infra-bot: Test harness started: ecc-smoke-2026-03-17 on host-g4-102, host-g4-103. monitor url: https://ci.redwood.example/tests/ecc-smoke-2026-03-17

maria: thanks — if we get a reproduction, let's also capture `pcie link status` and compare across kernel versions (5.15 vs 5.19 experimental). kernel difference might explain why Xid dropped but ECC rose.

liam: noted. I'll include `ethtool -i` and `lspci -vv` snapshots too. will report back with the 2h summary.

sasha: good plan. will hold the rest of the rollout for now. :white_check_mark:
